draft.title: Comparing texts
card: Comparing texts means looking at how two texts deal with the same idea. Both texts must be about that shared idea, such as bravery or change.
find what the texts share in how they treat the idea. This might be a similar message, a similar technique or a similar view.
find where the treatment is not the same. This might be a different message, tone, text type or point of view.
Then explain why. Purpose, audience and context often shape how a text treats an idea, so a good comparison links each difference to one of them.
draft.remember: Comparing means finding likenesses and differences in treating one idea, then explaining why.

a.q: Which is the best start to a comparison of two texts?
opts: Both texts explore loneliness, but they treat it differently
The first text is longer and has more paragraphs
The first text is a poem and the second is a story
Both texts are interesting and well written
a.why: A comparison starts from a shared idea and then looks at how the treatment is alike and different. Saying the texts are different forms is a point of difference, but it does not name a shared idea.
a.clue: Look for the option that names an idea both texts share.

b.q: Text A is a news report on a flood that treats the community's recovery in a calm, factual tone. Text B is a poem about a flood that treats it in an emotional tone. Which comparison best explains the difference?
opts: The report aims to inform, but the poem aims to stir feeling
The report is about a flood and the poem is about a flood
The report has more words, so it is the better text
The poem is about feelings, so it has no purpose
b.why: A strong comparison explains a difference by linking it to purpose. A report informs, so its tone is factual, while a poem often aims to stir feelings. Saying both are about floods only names the shared idea and does not explain the difference.
b.clue: Which option links the tone to what each text is trying to do?

a.best: Both texts explore loneliness, but they treat it differently

b.best: The report aims to inform, but the poem aims to stir feeling
